## TL;DR

Cleared the two open review findings and re-verified the implementation end to end. The branch no longer carries `work/engineering-reports/0997/round-1.json` (it was removed in `663be1963`; main never had it, so removing it is the correct shape, not restoring it). The Cancel capture was re-taken from the current tree, and `default-6.png` now visibly shows the board with the restart dialog dismissed. I re-ran all three declared shots locally, opened every PNG, and confirmed the hover reason, the open shared dialog and the closed-after-Cancel state. `repoos check --changed main` is the remaining gate.

## Work and rationale

The card's yellow line is built by `needsInputHint`. It previously used `needsInputBannerText`, the category text (“The agent exited with an error.”), while the drawer's Waiting-for-you row combined that banner with `needsInputDetail`. The fix routes the hint through `formatNeedsInputDetailForDisplay`, so the tooltip prefers the concrete detail and only falls back to the banner when no detail exists — one reason-formatting path rather than a second copy. The same detail line on the card moved from a native `title` to the shared `data-tip` tooltip, satisfying the no-native-tooltip rule and keeping focusable/keyboard behaviour.

The status line already had `role="button"`, `tabindex`, and Enter/Space handlers, but `onCardHintClick` only branched on coding, PM, moving and stuck states; `tc-needs-input` fell through and did nothing. It now calls the same `openTaskStatusDetails()` destination the drawer uses, so mouse and keyboard both open Status details.

The restart confirmation was a hand-rolled fixed overlay rendered inline inside the card column. It had no `data-overlay-layer`, so while a Radix dialog had `<body>` pointer-transparent its buttons lost hit-testing (#0575). It is now the shared `ui/dialog/*` primitives inside `<Teleport to="body">`, which supply the layer marker, focus trap, Escape handling and outside-click dismissal. Restart-specific layout now decorates the `cc-modal` shell.

## Approaches tried

For the tooltip I chose detail-first rather than banner-plus-detail: the acceptance criterion asks for the real reason with no generic fallback when one exists. For the dialog I considered only adding the layer marker to the old overlay, but kept the shared-dialog route because the task requires it and it fixes the stacking-context problem at the same time. For the review's Cancel finding I did not guess: I forced a local capture with `--viewport 1280x800` (the default remote capture timed out), then opened the new PNGs. That re-capture is what resolves the finding.

## Challenges and blockers

Default remote browser capture failed with “could not reach the RepoOS server: The operation timed out.” An explicit `--viewport` keeps the capture local, which succeeded and produced `default-4/5/6.png`. The regression test cannot hit-test pointer events in jsdom, so it asserts the two mechanics that broke: the dialog is teleported out of the card and both content and scrim carry the shared layer id. Real-browser evidence covers the click path.

The approval note on `src/server/task-watchdog.ts` (`handleStalledCleanExit`, landed via `7361989e3`) is unchanged — this branch makes no server change and needs no decision on it. The landing check's other edge case, an uncommitted `schedules/0012-daily-safe-worktree-cleanup.md` on main, is not this branch's file; the worktree diff touches no `schedules/` path.

## Key learnings

A visually correct overlay is not a clickable one: `data-overlay-layer` is part of the contract, not decoration. Evidence files are tied to the tree that produced them, so re-capturing after the fix is the only way to clear a stale-capture finding. A capture is taken before its assertion runs, so “closed” must be proven by looking at the PNG, not by a passing `count: 0`.
